newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: Austria couple guilty in child cancer tug-of-war.
newsitem.headline: Austria couple guilty in child cancer tug-of-war.

text.p: A young cancer patient's parents received suspended jail terms on Monday after an Austrian court found them guilty of injury through neglect for trying to deny their daughter life-saving treatment, television reported.

The court in Wiener Neustadt, outside Vienna, also found Helmut Pilhar, 31, and Erika Pilhar, 33, guilty of abducting their eight-year-old daughter Olivia in the summer of 1995 when she was in the care of the authorities.
Judge Wolfgang Jedlicka gave both parents an eight months' suspended prison sentence.
The Pilhars had refused chemotherapy for their daughter, who was suffering from abdominal cancer, on the advice of German "miracle curer" Ryke Gerd Hamer who advocates natural remedies.

The Pilhars fled to Malaga, Spain in July 1995 when the authorities issued an injunction against them. The case dominated Austrian media and President Thomas Klestil made a personal appeal to the couple to return home.
The Pilhars finally relented and soon after their arrival back in Vienna in August 1995 the authorities stripped them of custody and the battle to save Olivia's life began.

By then her tumour had grown to the size of a soccer ball, weighing 4.5 kg (nine pounds). But she defied the odds and responded to treatment. Within weeks she was off intensive care and doctors have recently declared her healthy.
